# Theme

The root component, the built-in theme, and the functions that build and compile themes into CSS variables.

## CSS_VAR_PREFIX

Prefix of every CSS variable of the library, `'--vl-'`: the token `color-accent` is the CSS variable
`--vl-color-accent`.

```ts
const CSS_VAR_PREFIX: "--vl-"
```

## compileTheme

Compiles a resolved theme into CSS variables. In order: the primitive tokens (such as `--vl-neutral-50`), the
semantic tokens with their derived states (`-hover`, `-active`, `-disabled`, `-subtle`, and readable `-text`
variants of the status colors), the viewer stage tokens, the theme's token overrides, and last the component
tokens for `options.density` (`comfortable` by default), which overrides cannot change. Returns an object of
variable names (with the `--vl-` prefix) → values; turn it into a style sheet with toCssText. A pure function: it
runs in the browser or in Node.

```ts
compileTheme(theme: Theme, options?: CompileOptions): CssVars
```

## cssVar

Returns the CSS expression that references a token: `cssVar('color-accent')` returns
`'var(--vl-color-accent)'`. `token` is the token name without the `--vl-` prefix; the name is not checked. Use it
where code needs a CSS value that follows the theme, such as the color of an SVG drawn in code.

```ts
cssVar(token: string): string
```

## extendTheme

Creates a new theme definition from an existing one, such as the built-in `defaultTheme` with a brand accent
color. `overrides.colors` applies to both color modes, `light` and `dark` to one mode (after `colors`), `scale`
replaces fields of the non-color tokens, and `tokens` overrides compiled tokens by name. Returns an
ExtendedThemeDefinition to pass to ThemeProvider's `theme`; `base` is not changed. It can be applied to its own
result: later overrides win, and the token overrides of `base` are kept.

```ts
extendTheme(base: ThemeDefinition | ExtendedThemeDefinition, overrides: ThemeOverrides): ExtendedThemeDefinition
```

## resolveTheme

Resolves a theme definition for one color mode: takes its `light` or `dark` colors and keeps the scale and the
token overrides. `def` is a ThemeDefinition or the result of extendTheme; `mode` is `light` or `dark` (resolve a
`system` preference yourself first). Returns a Theme, the input of compileTheme. ThemeProvider does this itself;
call it to compile CSS outside React, such as at build time or in tests.

```ts
resolveTheme(def: ThemeDefinition | ExtendedThemeDefinition, mode: ColorMode): Theme
```

## toCssText

Turns compiled CSS variables into style sheet text, such as `:root{--vl-color-accent:oklch(…);…}`. `vars` is
the result of compileTheme; `selector` is the selector of the rule, `:root` by default (pass another one, such as
`[data-brand]`, to apply a theme to part of the page). Returns one line of CSS for a `<style>` element or a file.

```ts
toCssText(vars: CssVars, selector?: string): string
```

## ThemeProvider

Root component of the design system: wrap the application once, outside App. It compiles the theme into CSS
variables (`--vl-*`) in a `<style id="vl-theme-vars">` element in the document head, sets `data-vl-theme`,
`data-vl-mode`, `data-vl-density` and `data-vl-reduced-motion` on `<html>`, configures the wrapped Ant Design
components from the same theme, and provides the language of the built-in texts. Color mode, density, viewer
background and language can be switched at runtime without reloading; useTheme reads and changes them. The styles
of the components still have to be imported once (`vellum-ui/styles.css`).

```ts
<ThemeProvider {...props} />
```

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `ThemeDefinition \| ExtendedThemeDefinition` | The theme, with its light and dark colors: `defaultTheme` by default, or your own created with extendTheme. Changing it at runtime recompiles the CSS variables. | `defaultTheme` | No |
| `colorMode` | `ColorModePreference` | Color mode preference (controlled): `light`, `dark` or `system`. Use it with `onColorModeChange` when the preference is stored elsewhere, such as in the user settings; without it, the preference is kept inside and starts at `defaultColorMode`. | — | No |
| `defaultColorMode` | `ColorModePreference` | Initial color mode preference (uncontrolled); `system` follows the operating system. | `'light'` | No |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | Density (controlled): `comfortable` or `compact`. Use it with `onDensityChange`, such as when the density is read from a setting of the device. | — | No |
| `defaultDensity` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | Initial density (uncontrolled). | `'comfortable'` | No |
| `defaultViewerStage` | `'mid' \| 'dark' \| 'black'` | Initial viewer background of Lightbox: `mid`, `dark` or `black`. Users can switch it in Lightbox, and code with `useTheme().setViewerStage`. | `'dark'` | No |
| `reducedMotion` | `boolean` | The in-app "reduce motion" switch: `true` turns off transitions and animations (the motion durations become 0 ms). The setting of the operating system always applies as well. Sets `data-vl-reduced-motion` on `<html>`. | `false` | No |
| `locale` | `LocaleName \| Messages` | Language: the built-in `en-US` or `zh-CN`, or the text table of a custom language (missing keys fall back to en-US). Also switches the locale of the wrapped Ant Design components and the global locale of dayjs (both are English for a custom text table). | `'en-US'` | No |
| `messages` | `Messages` | Overrides or adds individual texts on top of `locale`, such as `{ 'empty.description': 'No projects' }`. | — | No |
| `onColorModeChange` | `(mode: ColorModePreference) => void` | Called with the new preference when `useTheme().setColorMode` is called; with a controlled `colorMode`, update it here. | — | No |
| `onDensityChange` | `(density: Density) => void` | Called with the new density when `useTheme().setDensity` is called; with a controlled `density`, update it here. | — | No |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The application. | — | No |

## useTheme

Hook that reads and changes the current theme. Returns a ThemeContextValue: the resolved `theme`, the color mode
in effect (`mode`) and the preference (`colorMode`), `density`, `viewerStage`, the compiled `cssVars`, and the
setters `setColorMode`, `setDensity` and `setViewerStage`. Must be used inside ThemeProvider; throws otherwise.
Use it for theme, color mode and density switchers.

```ts
useTheme(): ThemeContextValue
```

## builtinThemes

The built-in themes by ID. There is one, `default` (the same object as `defaultTheme`).

```ts
const builtinThemes: Readonly<Record<'default', ThemeDefinition>>
```

## DEFAULT_THEME

ID of the default built-in theme, `'default'`: the key of `defaultTheme` in `builtinThemes`.

```ts
const DEFAULT_THEME: BuiltinThemeId
```

## defaultTheme

The built-in theme `default`: a neutral gray canvas with white surfaces and a blue accent color, in light and dark
mode. ThemeProvider uses it when no `theme` is given; start from it with extendTheme to create your own theme.

```ts
const defaultTheme: ThemeDefinition
```

## componentTokens

The component tokens for a density: sizes maintained by the library, such as `control-height-md` (32 px
comfortable, 28 px compact), table cell padding and the widths of panels. `density` is `comfortable` or
`compact`. Returns a new object of token names without the `--vl-` prefix → CSS values, some of which reference
semantic tokens (`var(--vl-space-2)`). compileTheme adds them last, so theme overrides do not change them; call it
yourself only to inspect the values.

```ts
componentTokens(density: Density): Record<string, string>
```

## primitives

The primitive tokens: the color palettes and the size scales of the default theme, named by value rather than by
use (`neutral[50]`, `blue[500]`, `spaceScale`). Components never use them directly, only the semantic tokens;
use them when defining a theme by hand. All primitive colors are also compiled to CSS variables, such as
`--vl-neutral-50` and `--vl-blue-500`.

```ts
const primitives.ACCENT_HUE: 263
const primitives.neutral: { readonly 0: Oklch; readonly 25: Oklch; readonly 50: Oklch; readonly 100: Oklch; readonly 150: Oklch; readonly 200: Oklch; readonly 300: Oklch; readonly 400: Oklch; readonly 500: Oklch; readonly 600: Oklch; readonly 700: Oklch; readonly 750: Oklch; readonly 800: Oklch; readonly 850: Oklch; readonly 900: Oklch; readonly 925: Oklch; readonly 950: Oklch; readonly 975: Oklch; }
const primitives.blue: { readonly 300: Oklch; readonly 400: Oklch; readonly 500: Oklch; readonly 550: Oklch; readonly 600: Oklch; }
const primitives.status: { readonly danger: Oklch; readonly warning: Oklch; readonly success: Oklch; readonly info: Oklch; }
const primitives.spaceScale: readonly [0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64]
const primitives.fontSizeScale: { readonly '2xs': 11; readonly xs: 12; readonly sm: 13; readonly md: 14; readonly lg: 16; readonly xl: 20; readonly '2xl': 24; readonly '3xl': 32; readonly '4xl': 44; }
const primitives.radiusScale: { readonly sm: 6; readonly md: 8; readonly lg: 12; readonly xl: 16; readonly '2xl': 20; readonly full: 999; }
const primitives.fontWeightScale: { readonly regular: 400; readonly medium: 500; readonly semibold: 600; readonly bold: 600; }
const primitives.primitiveColors: Record<string, Record<string | number, Oklch>>
```

## defaultScale

The non-color semantic tokens of the default theme: the font stacks of `fontStacks`, font sizes 11–44 px, spacing
on a 4 px grid (0–64 px), radii 6–20 px, transitions of 120 / 200 / 280 ms. Spread it to change single fields
when defining a theme by hand.

```ts
const defaultScale: SemanticScale
```

## fontStacks

The font stacks of the default theme (`heading`, `body`, `accent`, `mono`), as CSS `font-family` values. Only
open fonts under the SIL OFL are named: Inter (variable font) for Latin text, then Source Han Sans / Noto Sans CJK
for Chinese, then the system fonts of each platform; JetBrains Mono for IDs, code and API names. The fonts
themselves are loaded by `vellum-ui/fonts.css` (Inter and JetBrains Mono).

```ts
const fontStacks: { readonly heading: "'Inter Variable', 'Inter', 'Source Han Sans SC', 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei UI', 'PingFang SC', system-ui, sans-serif"; readonly body: "'Inter Variable', 'Inter', 'Source Han Sans SC', 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei UI', 'PingFang SC', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif"; readonly accent: "'Inter Variable', 'Inter', 'Source Han Sans SC', 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei UI', 'PingFang SC', sans-serif"; readonly mono: "'JetBrains Mono Variable', 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'SFMono-Regular', Consolas, monospace"; }
```

## viewerStages

All viewer backgrounds, from light to dark: `['mid', 'dark', 'black']`; Lightbox offers them in this order. Use it
to build your own background switcher with `useTheme().setViewerStage`.

```ts
const viewerStages: readonly ViewerStage[]
```

## viewerStageTokens

The default values of the viewer tokens, by name without the `--vl-` prefix: the backgrounds `viewer-bg-mid`,
`viewer-bg-dark` and `viewer-bg-black`, the text colors `viewer-text` and `viewer-text-muted`, the controls
`viewer-control-bg`, `viewer-control-bg-hover` and `viewer-control-border`, and `viewer-placeholder`. They have no
chroma, because a tinted background changes how the colors of images are perceived, and they do not change with
the color mode or the accent color. The object is frozen; to change a value, override the token in a theme
(`tokens` of extendTheme).

```ts
const viewerStageTokens: Readonly<Record<string, string>>
```

## Types

Types of this library used above. Import them with `import type { … } from 'vellum-ui'`.

### Theme

A theme resolved for one color mode by resolveTheme, the input of compileTheme. `useTheme().theme` is the current
one.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | ID of the theme definition, such as `default`. | — | Yes |
| `nameKey` | `string` | Text key of the display name of the theme. | — | Yes |
| `mode` | `'light' \| 'dark'` | The color mode the theme was resolved for. | — | Yes |
| `colors` | `SemanticColors` | The semantic colors of that mode. | — | Yes |
| `scale` | `SemanticScale` | The non-color semantic tokens. | — | Yes |
| `tokenOverrides` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | Compiled tokens to override, by name without the `--vl-` prefix; empty for a theme that was not extended. | — | Yes |

### CompileOptions

Options of compileTheme.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | Density of the component tokens (control heights, table cell padding and other sizes). | `'comfortable'` | No |

### CssVars

Compiled CSS variables, as returned by compileTheme: full variable names (with the `--vl-` prefix) → values,
such as `'--vl-color-accent': 'oklch(57% 0.215 263)'`.

```ts
type CssVars = Readonly<Record<string, string>>
```

### ThemeDefinition

A theme: semantic colors for light and for dark mode, plus the non-color tokens. Pass it to ThemeProvider's
`theme`; create variants of an existing theme with extendTheme.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Theme ID, such as `default`; written to `data-vl-theme` on `<html>`. | — | Yes |
| `nameKey` | `string` | Text key of the display name of the theme, such as `theme.default` ("Vellum"), for theme pickers. | — | Yes |
| `light` | `SemanticColors` | Semantic colors in light mode. | — | Yes |
| `dark` | `SemanticColors` | Semantic colors in dark mode. | — | Yes |
| `scale` | `SemanticScale` | Non-color semantic tokens: fonts, sizes, spacing, radius, motion. | — | Yes |

### ExtendedThemeDefinition

A theme definition created by extendTheme: a ThemeDefinition plus overrides of compiled tokens. Accepted wherever
a ThemeDefinition is (ThemeProvider's `theme`, resolveTheme, extendTheme).

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tokenOverrides` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | Compiled tokens to override, by name without the `--vl-` prefix: the `tokens` of all extendTheme calls, later ones winning. | — | Yes |
| `id` | `string` | Theme ID, such as `default`; written to `data-vl-theme` on `<html>`. | — | Yes |
| `nameKey` | `string` | Text key of the display name of the theme, such as `theme.default` ("Vellum"), for theme pickers. | — | Yes |
| `light` | `SemanticColors` | Semantic colors in light mode. | — | Yes |
| `dark` | `SemanticColors` | Semantic colors in dark mode. | — | Yes |
| `scale` | `SemanticScale` | Non-color semantic tokens: fonts, sizes, spacing, radius, motion. | — | Yes |

### ThemeOverrides

Changes to apply to a theme with extendTheme, such as a brand accent color. Every field is optional; what is not
given stays as in the base theme.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | ID of the new theme, written to `data-vl-theme` on `<html>`; the ID of the base theme by default. | — | No |
| `nameKey` | `string` | Text key of the display name of the new theme, looked up in the text table (add the text with ThemeProvider's `messages`); that of the base theme by default. | — | No |
| `colors` | `Partial<SemanticColors>` | Semantic colors for both color modes, such as a brand accent color. To change the accent color, set `accent`, `accentFill` and `accentText` together. | — | No |
| `light` | `Partial<SemanticColors>` | Semantic colors for light mode only; applied after `colors`. | — | No |
| `dark` | `Partial<SemanticColors>` | Semantic colors for dark mode only; applied after `colors`. | — | No |
| `scale` | `Partial<SemanticScale>` | Non-color semantic tokens to replace (fonts, sizes, spacing, radius, motion). Each field given replaces that field as a whole, such as the whole `radius` object. | — | No |
| `tokens` | `Readonly<Record<string, string>>` | Compiled tokens to override directly, by name without the `--vl-` prefix (such as `color-accent` or `viewer-bg-dark`), in both modes. Component tokens (control heights and other sizes that depend on the density) are not affected by overrides. | — | No |

### ColorMode

A resolved color mode: `light` or `dark`.

```ts
type ColorMode = 'light' | 'dark'
```

### ColorModePreference

The color mode chosen by the user: `light`, `dark`, or `system` to follow the setting of the operating system
(and to change with it).

Values: `"dark"`, `"light"`, `"system"`

### LocaleName

A built-in language: `en-US` (English, the default) or `zh-CN` (Simplified Chinese).

```ts
type LocaleName = 'en-US' | 'zh-CN'
```

### Messages

A text table: key → text. Texts may contain `{name}` placeholders, which formatMessage fills in. Used for the
`locale` and `messages` of ThemeProvider and LocaleProvider; the keys are the built-in `MessageKey`s, and other keys
(such as the `nameKey` of a custom theme) are allowed too.

```ts
type Messages = Readonly<Partial<Record<MessageKey, string>>> &
  Readonly<Record<string, string>>
```

### Density

Density of the interface: `comfortable` for everyday use, `compact` for data-dense screens that use tables a lot.
It changes the component tokens only: control heights, table cell padding and similar sizes.

```ts
type Density = 'comfortable' | 'compact'
```

### ThemeContextValue

The current theme and its setters, returned by useTheme.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `Theme` | The current theme, resolved for the current color mode. | — | Yes |
| `mode` | `Theme['mode']` | The color mode in effect, `light` or `dark` (`system` resolved from the setting of the operating system). | — | Yes |
| `colorMode` | `ColorModePreference` | The color mode preference of the user: `light`, `dark` or `system`. | — | Yes |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | The current density. | — | Yes |
| `viewerStage` | `'mid' \| 'dark' \| 'black'` | The current viewer background of Lightbox. | — | Yes |
| `cssVars` | `CssVars` | The CSS variables compiled for the current theme and density. | — | Yes |
| `setColorMode` | `(mode: ColorModePreference) => void` | Changes the color mode preference and calls `onColorModeChange`. With a controlled `colorMode`, the change takes effect when the new value is passed back. | — | Yes |
| `setDensity` | `(density: Density) => void` | Changes the density and calls `onDensityChange`. With a controlled `density`, the change takes effect when the new value is passed back. | — | Yes |
| `setViewerStage` | `(stage: ViewerStage) => void` | Changes the viewer background of Lightbox. The choice is not stored: it lasts while ThemeProvider is mounted. | — | Yes |

### BuiltinThemeId

ID of a built-in theme: `'default'`.

```ts
type BuiltinThemeId = keyof typeof builtinThemes
```

### SemanticScale

The non-color semantic tokens: fonts, sizes, spacing, radius, motion. A theme may replace them (`scale` of
extendTheme). Sizes are in pixels and durations in milliseconds.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fontFamilyHeading` | `string` | Font stack of headings (`font-family-heading`). | — | Yes |
| `fontFamilyBody` | `string` | Font stack of body text (`font-family-body`). | — | Yes |
| `fontFamilyAccent` | `string` | Font stack for accent text in applications (`font-family-accent`); the components do not use it. | — | Yes |
| `fontFamilyMono` | `string` | Monospace font stack, for IDs, code and API names (`font-family-mono`). | — | Yes |
| `fontSize` | `Readonly<Record<keyof typeof fontSizeScale, number>>` | Font sizes in pixels, `2xs` (11) to `4xl` (44); compiled to `font-size-<step>`. | — | Yes |
| `fontWeight` | `Readonly<Record<keyof typeof fontWeightScale, number>>` | Font weights: `regular`, `medium`, `semibold` and `bold`; compiled to `font-weight-<name>`. | — | Yes |
| `lineHeightBody` | `number` | Line height of body text, as a factor (`1.55`). | — | Yes |
| `lineHeightHeading` | `number` | Line height of headings, as a factor (`1.2`). | — | Yes |
| `space` | `readonly number[]` | Spacing steps in pixels, index 0–8; compiled to `space-0` … `space-8`. | — | Yes |
| `radius` | `Readonly<Record<keyof typeof radiusScale, number>>` | Corner radii in pixels: `sm` small controls, `md` controls, `lg` menus and messages, `xl` cards, `2xl` dialogs, `full` pills and circles; compiled to `radius-<name>`. | — | Yes |
| `borderWidth` | `number` | Width of borders and dividers in pixels. | — | Yes |
| `motionDurationFast` | `number` | Fast transitions such as hover, in milliseconds (`motion-duration-fast`). | — | Yes |
| `motionDurationBase` | `number` | Base transitions such as indicators and dialogs, in milliseconds (`motion-duration-base`). | — | Yes |
| `motionDurationSlow` | `number` | Slow transitions such as drawers and pages, in milliseconds (`motion-duration-slow`). | — | Yes |
| `motionEaseStandard` | `string` | Easing of most transitions, a CSS easing function (`motion-ease-standard`). | — | Yes |
| `motionEaseExit` | `string` | Easing of exit transitions, when an element leaves (`motion-ease-exit`). | — | Yes |
| `fontWeightHeading` | `number` | Font weight of headings. | — | Yes |
| `letterSpacingHeading` | `string` | Letter spacing of headings, a CSS length such as `-0.01em`. | — | Yes |
| `letterSpacingOverline` | `string` | Letter spacing of overlines (small group titles). | — | Yes |

### ViewerStage

A viewer background, the neutral background behind images in Lightbox: `mid` gray, `dark` gray or `black`.

```ts
type ViewerStage = 'mid' | 'dark' | 'black'
```

### SemanticColors

The semantic colors a theme provides for one color mode. These are base colors: the hover, active, disabled and
subtle variants are derived from them in OKLCH when the theme is compiled. Each field is compiled to
`color-<name in kebab case>`, such as `bgCanvas` → `--vl-color-bg-canvas`.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bgCanvas` | `Oklch` | Background of the page (the canvas). | — | Yes |
| `bgSurface` | `Oklch` | Surfaces such as cards and panels. | — | Yes |
| `bgElevated` | `Oklch` | Elevated surfaces: overlays such as menus, popovers and dialogs. | — | Yes |
| `bgSunken` | `Oklch` | Sunken areas that are deeper than the surface, such as code blocks and tracks. | — | Yes |
| `fill` | `Oklch` | Neutral fill of filled controls without a border: secondary buttons, inputs, the track of a segmented control. | — | Yes |
| `fillStrong` | `Oklch` | Stronger neutral fill: the track of a switch that is off, an unchecked checkbox. | — | Yes |
| `border` | `Oklch` | Divider lines, only between table rows and list items. | — | Yes |
| `borderStrong` | `Oklch` | Outline of the few controls that need one, such as outlined buttons. | — | Yes |
| `textPrimary` | `Oklch` | Main text color. | — | Yes |
| `textSecondary` | `Oklch` | Secondary text: descriptions, labels, metadata. | — | Yes |
| `textTertiary` | `Oklch` | Tertiary text: placeholders, hints, the least important information. | — | Yes |
| `textOnAccent` | `Oklch` | Text on the solid accent fill, such as on a primary button. | — | Yes |
| `accent` | `Oklch` | The only accent color: switches, indicators, focus rings, selection. | — | Yes |
| `accentFill` | `Oklch` | Solid accent fill: primary buttons, checked checkboxes. In dark mode it is darker than `accent`, so that white text keeps a contrast of at least 4.5:1. | — | Yes |
| `danger` | `Oklch` | Danger (destructive actions, errors). | — | Yes |
| `warning` | `Oklch` | Warning. | — | Yes |
| `success` | `Oklch` | Success. | — | Yes |
| `info` | `Oklch` | Information. | — | Yes |
| `shadow` | `Oklch` | Base color of shadows, with transparency. | — | Yes |
| `accentText` | `Oklch` | The accent color as text or icons on the canvas, such as links; easier to read than `accent`. | — | Yes |
| `avatar` | `readonly [ToneColors, ToneColors, ToneColors, ToneColors, ToneColors]` | The five avatar tones (blue, green, orange, purple, cyan): light backgrounds with dark text in light mode, dark backgrounds with light text in dark mode, no border. Avatar picks one stably from the name. Compiled to `color-avatar-1-bg` / `color-avatar-1-text` … `color-avatar-5-*`. | — | Yes |
| `chart` | `ChartColors` | Chart colors, see ChartColors. | — | Yes |

### Oklch

A color in OKLCH, the color space in which all colors of the library are defined: perceptually uniform, so colors
derived by changing the lightness look alike in light and dark mode. Create one with `oklch()`.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `l` | `number` | Lightness, 0 (black) to 1 (white). | — | Yes |
| `c` | `number` | Chroma, 0 (gray) to about 0.4 (the most saturated colors). | — | Yes |
| `h` | `number` | Hue angle in degrees, 0–360 (about 25 red, 150 green, 263 the blue of the default accent color). | — | Yes |
| `alpha` | `number` | Opacity, 0–1; opaque when omitted. | — | No |

### ToneColors

A pair of colors for a tinted element: a background and the text on it, with a contrast of at least 4.5:1
(WCAG AA). Used for the tones of Avatar.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bg` | `Oklch` | Background color. | — | Yes |
| `text` | `Oklch` | Color of the text and icons on the background. | — | Yes |

### ChartColors

Chart colors. Each kind of color has one job: categorical colors tell series apart, sequential colors show
magnitude, and diverging colors show on which side of a baseline a value is. Status (good / bad) is not here:
use the semantic `danger`, `warning` and `success` colors, always with an icon and text.

The default values are checked by the tests of the library (lightness range, minimum chroma, difference between
neighbors for color vision deficiencies, contrast with the surface). A theme that replaces them should meet the
same rules; do not pick them by eye.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `categorical` | `readonly [Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch]` | The 8 categorical colors, assigned to series in a fixed order: the n-th series always gets the n-th color, so hiding a series does not recolor the others. The order itself keeps neighbors distinguishable for color vision deficiencies; do not reorder. Compiled to `color-chart-1` … `color-chart-8`. | — | Yes |
| `sequential` | `readonly [Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch]` | The 7 sequential colors of one hue, ordered from the smallest to the largest value (light to dark in light mode, dark to light in dark mode). For continuous values such as a heatmap; ordered categories (funnel stages, levels) use only steps 3–7, which have a contrast of at least 2:1 with the surface. Compiled to `color-chart-seq-1` … `color-chart-seq-7`. | — | Yes |
| `diverging` | `readonly [Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch, Oklch]` | The 7 diverging colors: step 1 is the negative end, step 4 a neutral gray ("no deviation"), step 7 the positive end; the two ends have opposite (cool and warm) hues. Compiled to `color-chart-div-1` … `color-chart-div-7`. | — | Yes |
| `muted` | `Oklch` | Muted color: "Other", the series that are not highlighted, the history part of a sparkline. | — | Yes |
| `grid` | `Oklch` | Grid lines (1 px solid lines, not dashed). | — | Yes |
| `axis` | `Oklch` | The baseline of an axis. | — | Yes |
